name: Context Merge (Feature 2)
description: Implement context merge lifecycle operation. When two neighboring contexts have >70% signal ID overlap (rolling time window) and >80% assessment agreement (accept/reject decisions and familiarity scores on shared signals), they merge. Merge unions vector stores, deduplicates agents, takes max energy, updates neighbor topology. Also handles decay-to-fork handoff: when a decaying context's neighbor is about to fork into its territory, fold the decaying context into the new partition. Wired into lifecycle check in mesh/mesh.py at same cadence as fork/decay. Three-layer architecture: Layer 1 (Detection) with pure functions, Layer 2 (Execution) with pure computation + async application, Layer 3 (Lifecycle Integration) with async functions wired into mesh.py.

functions.name: compute_signal_overlap
functions.description: Layer 1 — Detection. Pure function. Computes the Jaccard-style signal ID overlap ratio between two sets of signal IDs. Returns |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|. Returns 0.0 if both sets are empty. This is the foundational overlap metric for merge detection.

inputs.name: signals_a
inputs.description: Signal IDs from the first context within the rolling time window.

inputs.name: signals_b
inputs.description: Signal IDs from the second context within the rolling time window.

postconditions: Result is in [0.0, 1.0].
If both inputs are empty, result is 0.0.
Result is symmetric: compute_signal_overlap(a, b) == compute_signal_overlap(b, a).
If signals_a == signals_b and both non-empty, result is 1.0.
Result equals len(set(signals_a) & set(signals_b)) / len(set(signals_a) | set(signals_b)) when union is non-empty.

functions.name: compute_assessment_agreement
functions.description: Layer 1 — Detection. Pure function. Computes the agreement ratio between two sets of assessments on shared signals. Two assessments on the same signal 'agree' if they have the same decision AND their familiarity scores are within epsilon of each other. Returns count_of_agreements / count_of_shared_signals. Returns 0.0 if there are no shared signals.

inputs.name: assessments_a
inputs.description: Assessments from the first context within the rolling window.

inputs.name: assessments_b
inputs.description: Assessments from the second context within the rolling window.

inputs.name: epsilon
inputs.description: Tolerance for familiarity score comparison. Two scores agree if abs(a - b) <= epsilon.

error_cases.name: duplicate_signal_in_assessments
error_cases.condition: A single assessment list contains multiple assessments for the same signal_id.

error_data.detail: Assessment list contains duplicate signal_id entries.

postconditions: Result is in [0.0, 1.0].
If there are no shared signals between the two assessment lists, result is 0.0.
Result is symmetric: compute_assessment_agreement(a, b, eps) == compute_assessment_agreement(b, a, eps).
If all shared signals have identical decisions and familiarity scores within epsilon, result is 1.0.

functions.name: detect_merge_candidates
functions.description: Layer 1 — Detection. Primary synchronous pure function for merge trigger detection. Iterates over all neighboring context pairs (each pair checked once), computes signal overlap via Jaccard similarity and assessment agreement on shared signals, and returns all pairs exceeding both thresholds as MergeCandidates ordered by combined_score descending. Only checks pairs that are declared neighbors — does not perform all-pairs comparison. Follows the existing fork/decay pattern in core/lifecycle.py.

inputs.name: signal_windows
inputs.description: Mapping of ContextId (str) -> SignalIdSet (frozenset[str]). Signal IDs per context within the rolling window.

inputs.name: assessments
inputs.description: Mapping of ContextId (str) -> Mapping[SignalId (str), AssessmentSummary]. Assessments per context per signal.

inputs.name: neighbors
inputs.description: Mapping of ContextId (str) -> NeighborSet (frozenset[str]). Neighbor topology.

inputs.name: overlap_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum Jaccard similarity to trigger merge. Strict inequality.

inputs.name: agreement_threshold
inputs.description: Minimum assessment agreement to trigger merge. Strict inequality.

error_cases.name: invalid_overlap_threshold
error_cases.condition: overlap_threshold < 0.0 or overlap_threshold > 1.0

error_data.message: overlap_threshold must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive, got {overlap_threshold}

error_cases.name: invalid_agreement_threshold
error_cases.condition: agreement_threshold < 0.0 or agreement_threshold > 1.0

error_data.message: agreement_threshold must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive, got {agreement_threshold}

error_cases.name: invalid_familiarity_score
error_cases.condition: Any AssessmentSummary in assessments has familiarity_score < 0.0 or familiarity_score > 1.0

error_data.message: familiarity_score must be between 0.0 and 1.0 inclusive for signal {signal_id} in context {context_id}

preconditions: overlap_threshold is a float in the range [0.0, 1.0].
agreement_threshold is a float in the range [0.0, 1.0].
All familiarity_score values within assessments are floats in [0.0, 1.0].
signal_windows, assessments, and neighbors are valid Mapping types (not None).
postconditions: The returned MergeDetectionResult contains only pairs where overlap > overlap_threshold AND agreement > agreement_threshold (strict inequality).
Each candidate pair appears at most once with context_id_a <= context_id_b lexicographically (canonical ordering).
Candidates are sorted by combined_score descending. Ties are broken deterministically by context_id_a then context_id_b ascending.
combined_score == overlap * agreement for every candidate.
Only neighboring pairs are evaluated — no non-neighbor pairs appear in results.
If signal_windows is empty, neighbors is empty, or no context has any neighbors, the result contains an empty candidates tuple.
The result is an immutable frozen Pydantic model.

functions.name: detect_decay_fold_candidates
functions.description: Layer 1 — Detection. Pure function. Scans a set of lifecycle proposals and context snapshots to detect decay-to-fork handoff scenarios: a context is DECAYING and a neighboring context is FORKING into its territory. Returns additional DECAY_FOLD merge proposals that should replace or supplement the original decay/fork proposals.

inputs.name: proposals
inputs.description: Current lifecycle proposals (fork, decay) collected in this cycle.

inputs.name: context_snapshots
inputs.description: Current state snapshots of all contexts in the mesh.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Merge configuration with thresholds and parameters.

postconditions: All returned proposals have kind == DECAY_FOLD.
Each returned proposal has exactly 2 affected_context_ids.
Each returned proposal has a non-None merge_proposal with is_decay_fold == true.
No returned proposal duplicates a pair already present in the input proposals.

functions.name: resolve_surviving_identity
functions.description: Layer 2 — Execution. Pure function. Determines which of two contexts survives a merge. The higher-energy context survives. On energy tie, the lexicographically smaller ID wins. Returns a tuple of (survivor_id, absorbed_id).

inputs.name: ctx_a
inputs.description: First context.

inputs.name: ctx_b
inputs.description: Second context.

error_cases.name: same_context_error
error_cases.condition: ctx_a.id == ctx_b.id

error_data.message: Cannot resolve surviving identity for the same context.

preconditions: ctx_a.id != ctx_b.id — contexts must be distinct.
postconditions: If ctx_a.energy > ctx_b.energy, returns ctx_a.
If ctx_b.energy > ctx_a.energy, returns ctx_b.
If ctx_a.energy == ctx_b.energy, returns the context with the lexicographically smaller id.
Result is deterministic: same inputs always produce the same survivor.

functions.name: deduplicate_agents
functions.description: Layer 2 — Execution. Pure function. Merges two agent lists, deduplicating by the (identity, role) composite key. On conflict (same key in both lists), the agent from the preferred context (higher-energy, or lexicographic tiebreak) is kept.

inputs.name: agents_a
inputs.description: Agents from the first context.

inputs.name: agents_b
inputs.description: Agents from the second context.

inputs.name: preferred_context_id
inputs.description: ID of the preferred context (higher energy / lexicographic winner) whose agents take precedence on conflict.

inputs.name: context_a_id
inputs.description: ID of the first context (owner of agents_a).

inputs.name: context_b_id
inputs.description: ID of the second context (owner of agents_b).

error_cases.name: invalid_preferred_context
error_cases.condition: preferred_context_id != context_a_id AND preferred_context_id != context_b_id

error_data.message: Preferred context ID must match one of the provided context IDs.

preconditions: preferred_context_id == context_a_id OR preferred_context_id == context_b_id.
postconditions: No two agents in the result have the same (identity, role) pair.
Every unique (identity, role) from agents_a and agents_b is represented in the result.
On conflict for a given (identity, role), the agent from the preferred context's agent list is in the result.
Result is deterministic: same inputs always produce the same output.

functions.name: merge_vector_stores
functions.description: Layer 2 — Execution. Async function. Unions two vector stores by delegating to the vector store's merge_union protocol method. Deduplicates entries by signal_id. Returns a new VectorStore instance with the surviving store's ID.

inputs.name: store_a
inputs.description: Vector store from the first context.

inputs.name: store_b
inputs.description: Vector store from the second context.

inputs.name: surviving_store_id
inputs.description: The store_id to assign to the resulting merged store.

error_cases.name: store_merge_failure
error_cases.condition: The underlying vector store merge_union protocol method raises an exception.

postconditions: result.store_id == surviving_store_id.
set(result.signal_ids) == set(store_a.signal_ids) | set(store_b.signal_ids) — the result is a union deduplicated by signal_id.
len(result.signal_ids) == len(set(result.signal_ids)) — no duplicate signal_ids in the result.

functions.name: compute_topology_updates
functions.description: Layer 2 — Execution. Pure function. Computes the list of TopologyUpdate commands needed to update the mesh topology after a merge. Produces remove_neighbor commands to remove the non-surviving context from all affected neighbors, and add_neighbor commands to introduce the surviving context to neighbors that only knew the non-surviving context.

inputs.name: surviving_id
inputs.description: ID of the surviving context.

inputs.name: removed_id
inputs.description: ID of the removed/absorbed context.

inputs.name: surviving_neighbor_ids
inputs.description: Neighbor IDs of the surviving context before merge.

inputs.name: removed_neighbor_ids
inputs.description: Neighbor IDs of the removed context before merge.

error_cases.name: same_id_error
error_cases.condition: surviving_id == removed_id

error_data.message: Surviving and removed context IDs must be distinct.

preconditions: surviving_id != removed_id — the two IDs must be distinct.
postconditions: For every neighbor N in removed_neighbor_ids where N != surviving_id, there is a REMOVE_NEIGHBOR command: (context_id=N, action=REMOVE_NEIGHBOR, target_id=removed_id).

For every neighbor N in removed_neighbor_ids where N != surviving_id AND N not in surviving_neighbor_ids, there is an ADD_NEIGHBOR command: (context_id=N, action=ADD_NEIGHBOR, target_id=surviving_id) AND (context_id=surviving_id, action=ADD_NEIGHBOR, target_id=N).
There is a REMOVE_NEIGHBOR command: (context_id=surviving_id, action=REMOVE_NEIGHBOR, target_id=removed_id) to clean the surviving context's own neighbor list.
No TopologyUpdate references surviving_id or removed_id as both context_id and target_id simultaneously in an ADD_NEIGHBOR command.

functions.name: merge
functions.description: Layer 2 — Execution. Async orchestrator function that executes the merge of two neighboring contexts into one. Resolves surviving identity, deduplicates agents, unions vector stores, takes max energy capped at system maximum, computes merged neighbor set, and returns a side-effect-free MergeResult with topology update commands. Located in core/lifecycle.py.

inputs.name: context_a
inputs.description: First context to merge.

inputs.name: context_b
inputs.description: Second context to merge.

inputs.name: reason
inputs.description: The reason for the merge. SIGNAL_OVERLAP for threshold-triggered merges, DECAY_FOLD for decay-to-fork handoff.

inputs.name: system_config
inputs.description: System-level configuration with max_energy cap.

error_cases.name: same_context_error
error_cases.condition: context_a.id == context_b.id

error_data.message: Cannot merge a context with itself.

error_cases.name: not_neighbors_error
error_cases.condition: context_b.id not in context_a.neighbor_ids OR context_a.id not in context_b.neighbor_ids

error_data.message: Contexts must be neighbors to merge.

error_cases.name: vector_store_merge_failure
error_cases.condition: The vector store's merge_union protocol method raises an exception during store union.

error_cases.name: invalid_energy_error
error_cases.condition: context_a.energy < 0.0 OR context_b.energy < 0.0

error_cases.name: invalid_system_config_error
error_cases.condition: system_config.max_energy <= 0.0

error_data.message: System max energy must be positive.

preconditions: context_a.id != context_b.id — the two contexts must be distinct.
context_b.id in context_a.neighbor_ids AND context_a.id in context_b.neighbor_ids — the two contexts must be neighbors.
context_a.energy >= 0.0 AND context_b.energy >= 0.0 — both contexts must have non-negative energy.
system_config.max_energy > 0.0 — system maximum energy must be positive.
postconditions: result.surviving_context_id == (context with higher energy).id, or lexicographically smaller ID if energies equal.
result.merged_energy == min(max(context_a.energy, context_b.energy), system_config.max_energy).
All agents from both contexts are represented in result.merged_agent_ids with no duplicates by (identity, role).
set(result.topology_patch.new_neighbors context_ids) is disjoint from {context_a.id, context_b.id}.
result.removed_context_id is the ID of the non-surviving context.
result.redirect.removed_context_id == result.removed_context_id.
result.redirect.surviving_context_id == result.surviving_context_id.
result.proposal preserves the merge reason for audit.
No side effects are applied — the returned MergeResult is purely descriptive.

functions.name: check_merges
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Pure function. Scans all pairs of neighboring contexts from snapshots and returns MergeProposals for pairs that exceed the overlap and agreement thresholds. This is the merge-specific proposal collection step within the lifecycle cycle. Skips contexts not in STABLE state.

inputs.name: context_snapshots
inputs.description: Current state snapshots of all contexts in the mesh.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Merge configuration with thresholds and parameters.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: Current lifecycle states of all contexts. Only STABLE contexts are considered.

postconditions: All returned proposals have overlap_score >= config.overlap_threshold and agreement_score >= config.agreement_threshold.
No proposal involves a context whose lifecycle_state is not STABLE.
Each unordered pair of contexts appears at most once in the result.
Proposals are ordered by combined score (overlap_score * agreement_score) descending.

functions.name: check_merge
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Pure function. Evaluates whether two specific neighboring contexts should merge based on signal overlap and assessment agreement thresholds defined in config. Returns a MergeProposal if both thresholds are met, or None otherwise.

inputs.name: context_a
inputs.description: First context snapshot.

inputs.name: context_b
inputs.description: Second context snapshot.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Merge configuration with thresholds.

error_cases.name: same_context
error_cases.condition: context_a.context_id == context_b.context_id

error_data.detail: Cannot check merge of a context with itself.

preconditions: context_a.context_id != context_b.context_id.
context_a and context_b are neighbors (context_b.context_id appears in context_a.neighbors or vice versa).
postconditions: If returned value is not None, then returned.overlap_score >= config.overlap_threshold and returned.agreement_score >= config.agreement_threshold.
If returned value is not None, source_context_id is the context with lower energy (tie-broken by lexicographic context_id), target_context_id is the other.
If returned value is None, at least one threshold was not met.

functions.name: resolve_lifecycle_conflicts
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Pure function. Given a list of all lifecycle proposals (fork, decay, merge, decay_fold), resolves conflicts where multiple proposals affect the same context. Priority order: FORK > MERGE/DECAY_FOLD > DECAY. Within same priority, earlier timestamps win. Returns a LifecyclePlan with accepted and rejected proposals.

inputs.name: proposals
inputs.description: All lifecycle proposals collected in this cycle (fork, decay, merge, decay_fold).

postconditions: Every proposal in the input appears in exactly one of accepted_proposals or rejected_proposals.
No two accepted proposals share any affected_context_id.
len(accepted_proposals) + len(rejected_proposals) == len(proposals).
All rejected proposals have an entry in conflict_reasons.
Within accepted proposals, higher-priority proposals were chosen over lower-priority ones for conflicting contexts.
Within same priority, earlier timestamp proposals were chosen over later ones.

functions.name: check_lifecycle_guard
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Pure function. Checks whether a context can transition to a new lifecycle state. Returns true if the context is currently STABLE (or not in the state map); false otherwise. This is the atomic guard that must be called within a single event-loop turn before setting the state.

inputs.name: context_id
inputs.description: The context ID to check.

inputs.name: desired_state
inputs.description: The lifecycle state the context wants to transition to. Must be FORKING, DECAYING, or MERGING.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: Current lifecycle states of all contexts.

error_cases.name: invalid_desired_state
error_cases.condition: desired_state is STABLE or MERGED, which are not valid transition targets.

error_data.detail: Cannot explicitly transition to STABLE or MERGED via guard check.

preconditions: desired_state is one of FORKING, DECAYING, MERGING.
postconditions: Returns true only if lifecycle_states[context_id] is STABLE or context_id is not in lifecycle_states.
Returns false if lifecycle_states[context_id] is FORKING, DECAYING, MERGING, or MERGED.

functions.name: transition_lifecycle_state
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Atomically transitions a context's lifecycle state in the state map. Must be called immediately after check_lifecycle_guard returns true, with no intervening await.

inputs.name: context_id
inputs.description: The context ID to transition.

inputs.name: new_state
inputs.description: The new lifecycle state to set.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The lifecycle state map to mutate.

error_cases.name: concurrent_state_change
error_cases.condition: The context's state changed between the guard check and this transition call.

error_data.detail: Lifecycle state changed concurrently; aborting transition.

preconditions: check_lifecycle_guard was called and returned true for this context_id immediately prior, OR new_state is STABLE (revert) or MERGED (post-merge).
postconditions: lifecycle_states[context_id] == new_state after call.
side_effects: Mutates lifecycle_states in place, setting lifecycle_states[context_id] = new_state.

functions.name: execute_merge
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Pure function. Given two context snapshots and an approved MergeProposal, computes the MergeResult describing the merged state. Unions signal ID sets, deduplicates agent lists, takes max energy, computes topology patch. Does not apply any changes; returns a result to be applied by the caller.

inputs.name: context_a
inputs.description: First context snapshot.

inputs.name: context_b
inputs.description: Second context snapshot.

inputs.name: proposal
inputs.description: The approved merge proposal.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Merge configuration for redirect TTL and other parameters.

error_cases.name: context_id_mismatch
error_cases.condition: The context snapshot IDs do not match the proposal's source and target IDs.

error_data.detail: Context snapshot IDs do not match proposal source/target IDs.

error_cases.name: zero_energy_contexts
error_cases.condition: Both contexts have energy <= 0.0, indicating they may both be decayed.

error_data.detail: Cannot merge two contexts with zero or negative energy.

preconditions: The set {context_a.context_id, context_b.context_id} == {proposal.source_context_id, proposal.target_context_id}.
proposal.overlap_score >= 0.0 and proposal.agreement_score >= 0.0.
postconditions: result.surviving_context_id == proposal.target_context_id.
result.removed_context_id == proposal.source_context_id.
result.merged_energy == max(context_a.energy, context_b.energy).
All agent IDs from both contexts appear in result.merged_agent_ids with no duplicates.
result.redirect.removed_context_id == result.removed_context_id.
result.redirect.surviving_context_id == result.surviving_context_id.
result.redirect.ttl_seconds == config.redirect_ttl_seconds.
result.topology_patch.surviving_context_id == result.surviving_context_id.
Neither surviving_context_id nor removed_context_id appear in topology_patch.new_neighbors context IDs.

functions.name: apply_merge_result
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Side-effectful async function. Applies a MergeResult to the mesh: updates the surviving context's agents, energy, and vector store; removes the source context; updates neighbor topology for all affected contexts; adds the redirect entry to the redirect map; transitions lifecycle states. This is the integration point in mesh/mesh.py.

inputs.name: merge_result
inputs.description: The merge result to apply.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The lifecycle state map to update.

inputs.name: redirect_map
inputs.description: The redirect map to add the new redirect entry to.

error_cases.name: surviving_context_not_found
error_cases.condition: The surviving context does not exist in the mesh.

error_data.detail: Surviving context not found in mesh.

error_cases.name: removed_context_not_found
error_cases.condition: The removed context does not exist in the mesh.

error_data.detail: Removed context not found in mesh.

error_cases.name: unexpected_lifecycle_state
error_cases.condition: Either context is not in MERGING state when apply is called.

error_data.detail: Context not in MERGING state; cannot apply merge result.

error_cases.name: merge_apply_failed
error_cases.condition: An unexpected error occurs during application (e.g., vector store error). Both contexts are reverted to STABLE.

error_data.detail: Merge application failed; contexts reverted to STABLE.

preconditions: lifecycle_states[merge_result.surviving_context_id] == MERGING.
lifecycle_states[merge_result.removed_context_id] == MERGING.
merge_result.surviving_context_id exists in the mesh.
merge_result.removed_context_id exists in the mesh.
postconditions: lifecycle_states[merge_result.surviving_context_id] == STABLE.
lifecycle_states[merge_result.removed_context_id] == MERGED.
redirect_map contains an entry for merge_result.removed_context_id.
The surviving context has the merged agents, energy, and updated neighbors.
The removed context is no longer active in the mesh.
side_effects: Mutates the surviving context's state (agents, energy, vector store, neighbors).
Removes the source context from the mesh.
Mutates lifecycle_states for both contexts (surviving -> STABLE, removed -> MERGED).
Adds a redirect entry to redirect_map.
Updates neighbor lists of third-party contexts per topology_patch.

functions.name: resolve_signal_redirect
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Pure function. Resolves a target context ID through the redirect map, following chains if necessary (a merged context may redirect to another merged context). Returns the final surviving context ID, or the original ID if no redirect exists. Enforces a maximum chain depth to prevent cycles.

inputs.name: target_context_id
inputs.description: The context ID to resolve (may be a removed/merged context).

inputs.name: redirect_map
inputs.description: The redirect map to look up.

inputs.name: max_depth
inputs.description: Maximum redirect chain depth to follow before raising an error.

error_cases.name: redirect_chain_too_deep
error_cases.condition: The redirect chain exceeds max_depth, indicating a possible cycle or excessively long chain.

error_data.detail: Redirect chain exceeded max_depth; possible cycle detected.

postconditions: Returned context ID is not a key in redirect_map (i.e., it is not a merged/removed context), OR max_depth was reached.
If target_context_id is not in redirect_map, it is returned unchanged.
The redirect chain is followed up to max_depth hops.

functions.name: cleanup_expired_redirects
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Side-effectful function. Removes expired redirect entries from the redirect map based on their TTL and the current time. Also removes the MERGED lifecycle state entry for cleaned-up contexts.

inputs.name: redirect_map
inputs.description: The redirect map to clean up (mutated in place).

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The lifecycle state map to clean up (mutated in place).

inputs.name: current_time
inputs.description: Current timestamp for TTL comparison. Must be comparable to MergeRedirect.created_at.

postconditions: All entries in redirect_map where (created_at + ttl_seconds) < current_time have been removed.
Corresponding MERGED entries in lifecycle_states have been removed.
Return value equals the number of entries removed.
side_effects: Mutates redirect_map by removing expired entries.
Mutates lifecycle_states by removing MERGED entries for cleaned-up contexts.

functions.name: run_lifecycle_cycle
functions.description: Layer 3 — Lifecycle Integration. Top-level async integration function called from mesh/mesh.py's lifecycle check loop. Orchestrates a complete lifecycle cycle: (1) snapshot all contexts, (2) collect fork/decay/merge proposals via check_merges, (3) detect decay-fold candidates via detect_decay_fold_candidates, (4) resolve conflicts via resolve_lifecycle_conflicts, (5) execute all accepted proposals (applying state guards, transitions, and side effects), (6) clean up expired redirects via cleanup_expired_redirects. Returns a LifecycleCycleReport of everything that happened. This is the single entry point wired into mesh.py at fork/decay cadence.

inputs.name: context_snapshots
inputs.description: Current state snapshots of all contexts in the mesh.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Merge configuration with thresholds and parameters.

inputs.name: lifecycle_states
inputs.description: The lifecycle state map (mutated during execution).

inputs.name: redirect_map
inputs.description: The redirect map (mutated during execution).

inputs.name: current_time
inputs.description: Current timestamp for proposal creation and TTL computation.

inputs.name: existing_proposals
inputs.description: Pre-existing fork/decay proposals from the existing lifecycle checks. Merged with newly detected merge proposals for unified conflict resolution.

error_cases.name: lifecycle_cycle_fatal
error_cases.condition: A catastrophic error prevents the cycle from completing (e.g., mesh state corruption). All in-progress transitions are best-effort reverted to STABLE.

error_data.detail: Fatal error during lifecycle cycle; best-effort revert performed.

postconditions: All accepted proposals have been executed or appear in report.errors with contexts reverted to STABLE.
report.plan.accepted_proposals and report.plan.rejected_proposals are disjoint and cover all collected proposals.
Expired redirects have been cleaned up.
No context is left in MERGING state after this function returns (either STABLE or MERGED).
report.redirects_cleaned >= 0.
side_effects: Mutates lifecycle_states for all affected contexts.
Mutates redirect_map (adds new redirects, removes expired ones).
Mutates mesh context state (agents, energy, vector stores, topology) for all executed proposals via apply_merge_result.
Removes contexts that were absorbed in merges.

invariants: A context may be in at most one LifecycleState transition at any time; concurrent FORKING, DECAYING, and MERGING on the same context are mutually exclusive.
After a merge completes, exactly one of the two input contexts survives; the other is removed and a redirect entry is added to the redirect map.
Redirect map entries have a finite TTL and are cleaned up after expiry; no unbounded growth.
All pure functions are deterministic and produce no side effects.
Fork, decay, and merge proposals collected in the same cycle are conflict-resolved before any execution begins.
Existing fork and decay lifecycle behavior is unchanged; all pre-existing lifecycle tests must pass.
Surviving identity resolution is deterministic: higher energy wins, lexicographic ID tiebreak on equal energy.
Agent deduplication is deterministic: given the same two agent lists and the same preferred context, the same deduplicated list is always produced.
The merged context's neighbor set never contains either of the original context IDs.
removed_context_ids always contains exactly one element — the non-surviving context's ID.
Energy in the merged context is always in the range [0.0, system_config.max_energy].

TopologyUpdate commands are self-consistent: every remove_neighbor for the removed context is paired with add_neighbor for the surviving context where the neighbor was not already connected to the survivor.
MergeReason is always preserved from input to output without modification.
Vector store union is commutative: merge(A, B) and merge(B, A) produce vector stores with identical signal_id sets.
MergeCandidate pairs use canonical ordering: context_id_a <= context_id_b lexicographically.
Thresholds use strict inequality for detection: overlap > threshold and agreement > threshold.
MergeConfig thresholds overlap_threshold and agreement_threshold default to 0.7 and 0.8 respectively but are configurable.
The lifecycle_states dict is the single source of truth for context lifecycle state.
No context is left in MERGING state after run_lifecycle_cycle returns (either STABLE or MERGED).
requires: mesh/mesh.py lifecycle check loop must call run_lifecycle_cycle at the same cadence as fork/decay checks
Vector stores must implement a merge_union protocol method for union + dedup by signal_id
All context snapshots must be available synchronously at the start of a lifecycle cycle
Lifecycle state transitions must occur within a single event-loop turn with no await between check and set
